issb.title: Same reporting entity as the financial statements
issb.requirement: Sustainability-related financial disclosures must be for the same reporting entity as the related general purpose financial statements; a group that prepares consolidated statements reports on the consolidated group.
issb.gap: BRSR A.13 lets the filer choose a standalone or consolidated boundary, and many listed groups file a standalone BRSR alongside consolidated financial statements. A.23 only lists group entities and whether they join BR initiatives; it does not bring their data into the metrics.
issb.investorNote: Investors read sustainability metrics against the same group whose earnings and balance sheet they value, so a standalone BRSR for a group with large subsidiaries understates its exposures.

issb.title: Connected information
issb.requirement: Information must let users understand connections between sustainability-related risks and opportunities, between governance, strategy, risk management and metrics disclosures, and with the financial statements, using data and assumptions consistent with the financial statements as far as possible.
issb.gap: A.26 asks for the positive or negative financial implication of each material issue, but BRSR has no requirement to cross-reference financial-statement line items, explain differences in assumptions, or link governance, strategy and metrics disclosures to each other.
issb.investorNote: Investors want to trace a sustainability risk to the provision, impairment, capex or revenue line it affects in the accounts.

issb.ref: IFRS S1 para 64 (first-year relief: Appendix E para E4)
issb.title: Timing: report with the financial statements, same period
issb.requirement: Report sustainability-related financial disclosures at the same time as the related financial statements, covering the same reporting period (first-year relief allows later publication).
issb.investorNote: Releasing sustainability data with the annual accounts lets investors price both at the same time rather than months apart.

issb.title: Materiality (investor-focused)
issb.requirement: Disclose material information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity's prospects; information is material if omitting, misstating or obscuring it could reasonably be expected to influence primary users' decisions.
issb.gap: BRSR is a prescribed checklist: every Essential indicator is answered regardless of materiality, and materiality appears only in A.26 (list of material issues) and the Reg 30 threshold in P1 E2. ISSB needs a documented, investor-focused materiality judgement that drives what is disclosed and allows immaterial items to be omitted.
issb.investorNote: Investors want the company's own judgement of which sustainability issues move enterprise value, not only a compliance list.

issb.ref: IFRS S1 paras 70-71 (first-year relief: para E3)
issb.title: Comparative information
issb.requirement: Provide comparative information for the preceding period for all amounts disclosed, and for narrative information where useful; revise comparatives when prior-period estimates are updated.
issb.gap: Most BRSR quantitative tables carry current and previous FY columns, but some do not (e.g. P2.L5, P3.E14, P5.E10), there is no rule for narrative comparatives, and no rule for revising prior-period estimates or correcting errors (IFRS S1 paras 83-86).
issb.investorNote: Trend data is what lets investors judge whether performance is improving; restated comparatives keep those trends honest.

issb.title: Sources of guidance, incl. SASB Standards
issb.requirement: To identify sustainability-related risks and opportunities and the applicable disclosures, the entity must refer to and consider the applicability of the SASB Standards' disclosure topics and metrics, and may consider CDSB guidance, other investor-focused standard-setters, industry peers, GRI and ESRS.
issb.gap: BRSR is organised by the nine NGRBC principles and does not reference SASB industry topics or metrics; B.4 only lists certifications and standards adopted (ISO, SA 8000, BIS).
issb.investorNote: SASB industry metrics are the common yardstick global investors use to compare companies within a sector.

issb.title: Explicit and unreserved statement of compliance
issb.requirement: An entity whose disclosures comply with all requirements of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards must make an explicit and unreserved statement of compliance (and may not make it otherwise).
issb.gap: BRSR has no statement of compliance with an external standard; BRSR compliance is a legal filing obligation under LODR Reg 34(2)(f), not an ISSB claim.
issb.investorNote: Only an unreserved statement tells investors that every ISSB requirement, not a selection, has been applied.

issb.title: Judgements, measurement uncertainty and errors
issb.requirement: Disclose judgements with the most significant effect on the disclosures, the sources of measurement uncertainty for reported amounts, and correct material prior-period errors.
issb.gap: No BRSR question asks for judgements, measurement uncertainty or error correction. The nearest duties sit outside the questions: circular 2023/122 para 3.2 (disclose changes or industry-specific adjustments / estimations to the BRSR Core base methodology) and para 4.3 (scope, assumptions and estimates for value-chain data).
issb.investorNote: Estimated figures such as Scope 3 or water consumption are only decision-useful when investors know how uncertain they are.

issb.title: Governance body oversight of sustainability risks
issb.requirement: Identify the governance body or individual overseeing sustainability-related risks and opportunities, and describe how responsibilities are reflected in terms of reference, how skills and competencies are ensured, how and how often it is informed, how it considers these risks in strategy, major transactions and risk management, and how it oversees targets, including links to remuneration.
issb.gap: BRSR names the highest authority for BR policies (B.8), any sustainability committee (B.9) and who reviews NGRBC performance and how often (B.10). It does not ask about terms of reference, board competence, information flows, how sustainability enters strategic decisions, or whether targets feed remuneration.
issb.investorNote: Investors judge whether the board can actually challenge management on sustainability risks, not just whether a committee exists.

issb.title: Management's role, controls and procedures
issb.requirement: Describe management's role in governing sustainability-related risks and opportunities, including whether it is delegated to a specific management-level position or committee, and whether and how controls and procedures support oversight and are integrated with other internal functions.
issb.gap: BRSR identifies a responsible director and review frequency but does not ask about management-level controls and procedures over sustainability data or their integration with internal financial controls.
issb.investorNote: Controls over sustainability data are the precondition for assurance-grade numbers.

issb.title: Sustainability risks and opportunities and time horizons
issb.requirement: Describe the sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity's prospects, the short, medium and long-term horizons over which effects are expected, and how those horizons are defined and linked to planning.
issb.gap: A.26 lists material issues with risk/opportunity flag, rationale and mitigation, but does not require time horizons, their definitions, or the link to strategic planning cycles.
issb.investorNote: Knowing when a risk could bite tells investors whether it matters for this valuation horizon or a later one.

issb.title: Effects on business model and value chain
issb.requirement: Describe current and anticipated effects of sustainability-related risks and opportunities on the business model and value chain, and where in the business model and value chain they are concentrated (e.g. geographies, facilities, asset types).
issb.gap: A.26 gives issue-level rationale only. BRSR's value-chain questions (P3.L5, P5.L4, P6.L6, P6.L7) look at the entity's impacts on and assessments of partners, not at where risks to the entity are concentrated.
issb.investorNote: Concentration of risk in a few plants, crops or regions is what can turn a sustainability issue into an earnings event.

issb.title: Effects on strategy and decision-making
issb.requirement: Describe how the entity has responded to and plans to respond to sustainability-related risks and opportunities in its strategy and decision-making, progress against plans disclosed previously, and trade-offs considered.
issb.gap: B.5-B.7 cover commitments, targets, performance and a director's statement, but not how risks changed strategy, resource allocation or trade-offs between risks and opportunities.
issb.investorNote: Investors look for evidence that sustainability findings change capital allocation, not only reporting.

issb.title: Current and anticipated financial effects
issb.requirement: Disclose quantitative and qualitative information on how sustainability-related risks and opportunities affected financial position, performance and cash flows in the period, those with a significant risk of material adjustment next year, and how financial position, performance and cash flows are expected to change over the short, medium and long term.
issb.gap: A.26 only asks to indicate positive or negative financial implications per material issue. There is no quantification, no link to carrying amounts, and no anticipated effects by time horizon.
issb.investorNote: Financial effects are the bridge between a sustainability issue and the investor's valuation model.

issb.title: Resilience of strategy and business model
issb.requirement: Provide a qualitative and, if applicable, quantitative assessment of the resilience of the entity's strategy and business model to its sustainability-related risks.
issb.gap: BRSR has no resilience assessment. P6.L5 (business continuity and disaster management plan) concerns operational continuity, not strategic resilience.
issb.investorNote: Resilience analysis shows whether the business model still works under plausible adverse conditions.

issb.title: Risk management processes
issb.requirement: Describe the processes and policies used to identify, assess, prioritise and monitor sustainability-related risks (inputs, parameters, use of scenario analysis, likelihood and magnitude, prioritisation versus other risks, monitoring, changes from the prior period), the processes for opportunities, and how these are integrated into overall risk management.
issb.gap: BRSR asks for mitigation approach per material issue (A.26), review of NGRBC policies (B.10) and a BCP (P6.L5), but not the identification and assessment process or its integration with enterprise risk management. The Risk Management Committee mandate under LODR (which covers sustainability / ESG risks) sits outside BRSR and is a ready source.
issb.investorNote: Investors want to know that sustainability risks go through the same risk machinery as financial and operational risks.

issb.title: Metrics for each material risk and opportunity
issb.requirement: For each material sustainability-related risk or opportunity, disclose metrics required by an IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard and metrics the entity uses to measure and monitor it (including SASB-derived metrics), with definitions, methodology and any third-party validation for entity-specific metrics.
issb.gap: BRSR prescribes a fixed metric set by principle rather than metrics tied to each material risk, and does not ask for metric definitions or validation except through BRSR Core assessment / assurance.
issb.investorNote: Comparable, well-defined metrics are what let investors benchmark a company against peers.

issb.title: Targets: definition, progress and revisions
issb.requirement: For targets set or required by law, disclose the metric, objective, scope, period, base period, milestones, performance against target with trend analysis, and any revisions with reasons.
issb.gap: B.5 and B.6 are free text. BRSR does not require base period, milestones, the metric used, or explanation of target revisions.
issb.investorNote: Structured target data lets investors test credibility and track delivery year on year.

issb.title: Climate governance: board oversight and management role
issb.requirement: Describe the body or individual overseeing climate-related risks and opportunities (terms of reference, skills and competencies, how and how often informed, consideration in strategy and major transactions, oversight of climate targets and link to remuneration) and management's role, including controls and procedures.
issb.gap: BRSR identifies the BR head and sustainability committee but nothing climate-specific: no climate competence, frequency of climate briefings, oversight of climate targets or link to remuneration.
issb.investorNote: Investors expect climate to be on the board agenda with clear accountability, not delegated to a sustainability team alone.

issb.title: Climate risks (physical / transition), opportunities, horizons
issb.requirement: Describe climate-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects, classify each risk as physical or transition, state the time horizons over which effects could occur, and how short, medium and long term are defined and linked to planning horizons.
issb.gap: A.26 may list climate as a material issue but does not require physical/transition classification, time horizons or their definitions. Under IFRS S2 para 12 the entity must also consider the industry-based guidance topics.
issb.investorNote: Separating physical from transition risk tells investors whether the exposure is about assets and supply (weather) or about policy, prices and demand.

issb.title: Climate effects on business model and value chain
issb.requirement: Describe the current and anticipated effects of climate-related risks and opportunities on the business model and value chain, and where they are concentrated.
issb.gap: No BRSR question asks where climate risks are concentrated (e.g. crop-growing regions, coastal plants, energy-intensive lines). A.26 gives issue-level rationale only.
issb.investorNote: For a food processor, climate exposure usually concentrates in a few agricultural inputs and sourcing regions, which investors want to see named.

issb.title: Strategy response and climate transition plan
issb.requirement: Describe how the entity has responded and plans to respond to climate risks and opportunities: changes to the business model and resource allocation, direct and indirect mitigation and adaptation (own operations, customers and supply chain), any climate transition plan with key assumptions and dependencies, and how it plans to achieve its climate targets.
issb.gap: BRSR asks for GHG reduction projects (P6.E8), resource-efficiency initiatives (P6.L4) and commitments (B.5), but not a transition plan, its assumptions and dependencies, adaptation plans or resource allocation.
issb.investorNote: The transition plan is how investors test whether decarbonisation targets are funded and achievable.

issb.title: Resourcing of climate plans and progress on prior plans
issb.requirement: Describe how the entity is resourcing and plans to resource its climate response, and give quantitative and qualitative information on progress of plans disclosed in prior periods.
issb.gap: B.6 is a free-text performance statement; P2.E1 gives the share of R&D and capex in technologies improving environmental and social impact, which is neither climate-specific nor linked to a plan.
issb.investorNote: Investors compare promised climate spending with actual delivery to judge management credibility.

issb.title: Current financial effects of climate risks
issb.requirement: Disclose how climate-related risks and opportunities affected financial position, performance and cash flows in the reporting period, and those with a significant risk of material adjustment to carrying amounts of assets and liabilities within the next annual reporting period.
issb.gap: A.26 only flags positive or negative implications. No quantification, and no link to carrying amounts (impairment, useful lives, provisions, insurance costs).
issb.investorNote: Current-period effects show investors that climate is already in the numbers, not only a future scenario.

issb.title: Anticipated financial effects (short, medium, long term)
issb.requirement: Disclose how the entity expects its financial position (given investment and disposal plans and planned funding) and its financial performance and cash flows to change over the short, medium and long term given its climate strategy; quantitative unless the proportionality exemptions apply.
issb.gap: Nothing in BRSR is forward-looking in financial terms. The sign-only 'financial implications' column in A.26 is the only related hook and does not meet paras 16(c)-(d).
issb.investorNote: Anticipated effects are what investors feed into forecasts and cost-of-capital assumptions.

issb.title: Climate resilience and scenario analysis
issb.requirement: Use climate-related scenario analysis, commensurate with the entity's circumstances, to assess climate resilience: implications for strategy, significant uncertainties and capacity to adapt (22(a)); and how and when the analysis was done, including scenarios used (whether a 1.5°C-aligned scenario), time horizons, operations covered and key assumptions (22(b)).
issb.gap: BRSR has no scenario analysis or resilience requirement. P6.L5 (business continuity and disaster management plan) is not a substitute.
issb.investorNote: Scenario analysis is the main evidence investors have that the strategy holds up under both a fast transition and severe physical change.

issb.title: Climate risk management processes
issb.requirement: Describe processes and policies to identify, assess, prioritise and monitor climate-related risks, including whether and how climate-related scenario analysis informs identification; processes for climate-related opportunities; and integration into overall risk management.
issb.gap: As for S1.rm, with no climate-specific process disclosure and no use of scenario analysis. The LODR Risk Management Committee's ESG-risk mandate is an input that BRSR does not report.
issb.investorNote: Investors want climate handled inside enterprise risk management, with the same rigour as credit or market risk.

issb.title: Scope 1 GHG emissions (absolute gross)
issb.requirement: Disclose absolute gross Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions for the reporting period, in metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
issb.investorNote: Scope 1 is the baseline for carbon-price exposure and the anchor of any decarbonisation target.

issb.title: Scope 2 location-based plus contractual-instrument info
issb.requirement: Disclose absolute gross Scope 2 emissions on a location-based basis, and provide information about any contractual instruments (e.g. RECs, green tariffs, PPAs) necessary to inform users' understanding of Scope 2 emissions.
issb.gap: BRSR P6.E7 has a single 'Total Scope 2 emissions' line with no method label; the ISF standard (secondary reading) specifies the CEA grid factor, which in effect yields a location-based figure. There is no disclosure of the instruments behind renewable claims (open-access PPA, green tariff, I-RECs) or of a market-based figure; P6.E1 shows renewable electricity but not how it is sourced.
issb.investorNote: Investors need to see how much of a renewable-electricity claim rests on certificates rather than physical supply.

issb.ref: IFRS S2 para 29(a)(i)(3) and 29(a)(vi); transition relief para C4(b)
issb.title: Scope 3 GHG emissions by GHG Protocol category
issb.requirement: Disclose absolute gross Scope 3 emissions and the categories included, per the GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard, using the Scope 3 measurement framework; relief from disclosure in the first annual reporting period only.
issb.gap: BRSR asks for Scope 3 only as a Leadership (voluntary) indicator, as a single total with optional gas break-up and intensity; no category breakdown, no measurement approach, and it is outside BRSR Core assessment / assurance.
issb.investorNote: Scope 3 is usually most of a food company's footprint (agricultural ingredients, packaging, logistics) and drives transition risk in the supply chain.

issb.ref: IFRS S2 para 29(a)(ii)-(iii); amended by 'Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures' (Dec 2025, effective 1 Jan 2027)
issb.title: GHG Protocol measurement, approach, inputs, GWPs
issb.requirement: Measure GHG emissions under the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004) unless a jurisdictional authority or listing exchange requires another method, and disclose the measurement approach, inputs and assumptions (consolidation approach, emission factors, reasons for choices and changes). GWPs: latest IPCC assessment, with a jurisdictional relief added by the December 2025 amendments.
issb.gap: BRSR does not name the GHG Protocol or ask for the consolidation approach (operational / financial control, equity share), emission factors or GWP set. BRSR Core and the ISF standard give a base methodology and require deviations to be disclosed. Whether the SEBI / ISF methodology counts as a 'jurisdictional requirement' for the relief is a judgement for the preparer and assurer.
issb.investorNote: Method disclosure is what makes emissions comparable across companies and countries.

issb.title: Scope 1 and 2 split: consolidated group vs other investees
issb.requirement: Disaggregate Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated accounting group and other investees (associates, joint ventures, unconsolidated subsidiaries).
issb.gap: No BRSR equivalent. A.13 sets a standalone or consolidated boundary and A.23 lists associates and JVs, but no emissions split is asked.
issb.investorNote: The split shows investors which emissions sit inside the balance sheet they are valuing.

issb.title: Assets / activities vulnerable to transition risks
issb.requirement: Disclose the amount and percentage of assets or business activities vulnerable to climate-related transition risks.
issb.gap: BRSR has no such metric. P6.E2 identifies sites that are designated consumers under the PAT scheme, one indicator of regulatory transition exposure; there are no asset amounts or percentages, and status under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is not asked.
issb.investorNote: This metric sizes how much of the asset base could be stranded or repriced by carbon policy.

issb.title: Assets / activities vulnerable to physical risks
issb.requirement: Disclose the amount and percentage of assets or business activities vulnerable to climate-related physical risks.
issb.gap: P6.L1 (Leadership, voluntary) identifies facilities in water-stressed areas and their water flows. There is no hazard screening for heat, flood or cyclone, and no asset values or percentages.
issb.investorNote: Physical exposure of plants and sourcing regions drives insurance cost, downtime and input-price risk.

issb.title: Assets / activities aligned with climate opportunities
issb.requirement: Disclose the amount and percentage of assets or business activities aligned with climate-related opportunities.
issb.gap: No BRSR metric of revenue or assets aligned with climate opportunities. P2.E1 (R&D / capex share) and P9.E2 (products carrying information) do not measure alignment.
issb.investorNote: Investors look for the upside: revenue that grows as the economy decarbonises.

issb.title: Capital deployment towards climate risks and opportunities
issb.requirement: Disclose the amount of capital expenditure, financing or investment deployed towards climate-related risks and opportunities.
issb.gap: P2.E1 gives the percentage of R&D and capex in technologies that improve environmental and social impacts. It is not an amount, not climate-specific, and excludes financing and investments. P6.E8 lists GHG projects without amounts.
issb.investorNote: Capital deployment shows whether money is following the stated climate strategy.

issb.title: Internal carbon price
issb.requirement: Explain whether and how the entity applies a carbon price in decision-making (e.g. investment, transfer pricing, scenario analysis) and the price per metric tonne of GHG emissions used.
issb.gap: No BRSR question on internal carbon pricing.
issb.investorNote: An internal carbon price shows investors that projects are screened against future carbon costs.

issb.title: Climate-linked executive remuneration
issb.requirement: Describe whether and how climate-related considerations are factored into executive remuneration, and the percentage of executive management remuneration recognised in the period that is linked to climate-related considerations.
issb.gap: BRSR P5.E3 gives median remuneration by category and B.9 the sustainability committee, but nothing links pay to climate.
issb.investorNote: Pay linked to climate targets signals that management is accountable for delivering them.

issb.ref: IFRS S2 para 32 (and para 12); Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2
issb.title: Industry-based climate metrics
issb.requirement: Disclose industry-based metrics associated with the entity's business model and activities, referring to and considering the applicability of the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2 (for Processed Foods: energy management, water management and ingredient sourcing).
issb.gap: BRSR covers energy and water totals, and water stress only as a voluntary Leadership item. It has no ingredient-sourcing metrics (see the FB-PF rows).
issb.investorNote: Industry metrics let investors compare like with like within the food sector.

issb.title: Climate targets: definition, validation, performance
issb.requirement: Disclose climate-related targets set and required by law: metric, objective (mitigation, adaptation, science-based), part of the entity covered, period, base period, milestones, absolute or intensity, how the latest international climate agreement informed it; whether third-party validated, review process, revisions; performance and trends.
issb.gap: B.5 and B.6 are free text with no structured base year, milestones, validation status, revision history or explanation of Paris alignment.
issb.investorNote: Investors screen for targets that are specific, validated and tracked, rather than aspirational statements.

issb.title: GHG target details: gases, scopes, gross vs net, method
issb.requirement: For each GHG emissions target, disclose the gases covered, whether Scope 1, 2 or 3 is covered, whether it is a gross or net target (with the associated gross target if net), and whether it was derived using a sectoral decarbonisation approach.
issb.gap: B.5 does not ask for scope coverage, gases, gross versus net, or the method (e.g. SBTi sectoral pathway).
issb.investorNote: Without scope coverage and gross/net detail investors cannot tell what a 'net zero' target actually commits to.

issb.title: Planned use of carbon credits
issb.requirement: For net GHG targets, disclose the planned use of carbon credits: extent of reliance, the third-party schemes verifying or certifying them, the type (nature-based or technological; removal or reduction) and other factors on credibility and integrity (e.g. permanence).
issb.gap: BRSR has no carbon-credit disclosure. P6.L8 covers Green Credits under India's Green Credit Rules, 2023, which reward environmental actions (plantation, water, waste); they are not GHG offsets and do not meet para 36(e). Carbon credit certificates under India's CCTS are not asked about either.
issb.investorNote: Heavy reliance on low-quality offsets is a reputational and transition risk investors want to size.

issb.ref: SASB FB-PF-130a.1 (IFRS S2 para 32 / Industry-based Guidance; IFRS S1 para 55)
issb.title: Energy management: energy, % grid, % renewable
issb.requirement: Disclose (1) operational energy consumed (GJ), (2) percentage grid electricity and (3) percentage renewable.
issb.gap: P6.E1 gives total energy and the renewable / non-renewable split, but not the grid-electricity share (grid and captive fossil electricity are combined); SASB's renewable definition (incl. treatment of certificates) may differ from BRSR filers' practice.
issb.investorNote: Energy use and grid dependence drive exposure to power-tariff and carbon-cost increases in frying, baking and drying.

issb.title: Water withdrawn/consumed and % in high water stress
issb.requirement: Disclose (1) total water withdrawn and (2) total water consumed (thousand m3), and the percentage of each in regions with High or Extremely High Baseline Water Stress.
issb.gap: P6.E3 covers withdrawal by source and consumption (kL). The water-stress split is only in P6.L1, a Leadership (voluntary) item with no prescribed screening tool (SASB uses WRI Aqueduct baseline water stress).
issb.investorNote: Water-stressed sites face licence limits and cost spikes that can stop production lines.

issb.ref: SASB FB-PF-140a.2 (IFRS S1 para 55; inclusion in the IFRS S2 Industry-based Guidance not confirmed)
issb.title: Water-permit non-compliance incidents
issb.requirement: Disclose the number of incidents of non-compliance associated with water quality permits, standards and regulations.
issb.gap: P6.E13 is a Yes/No compliance statement with details of non-compliances, fines and corrective action, but no count of incidents and no split for water-quality permits.
issb.investorNote: Discharge non-compliance can lead to closure orders under the Water Act, a direct production risk.

issb.title: Water management risks and mitigation strategy
issb.requirement: Describe water management risks associated with withdrawals, consumption and discharge, and the strategies and practices to mitigate them.
issb.gap: BRSR covers ZLD implementation (P6.E5), initiatives (P6.L4) and, if material, water in A.26, but does not ask for a water-risk description by site or the mitigation strategy as such.
issb.investorNote: Investors want to know whether water constraints are being managed before they bite.

issb.title: Food safety: GFSI audit results and certified suppliers
issb.requirement: Disclose the Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) audit (1) non-conformance rate and (2) associated corrective action rate for major and minor non-conformances, and the percentage of ingredients sourced from Tier 1 supplier facilities certified to a GFSI-recognised food safety programme.
issb.gap: No BRSR equivalent. B.4 may list FSSC 22000 or similar certifications qualitatively; P2.E2 'sustainable sourcing' is not food-safety certification.
issb.investorNote: Food-safety failures are the fastest route to recalls, lost listings and brand damage.

issb.title: Food safety: violation notices and recalls
issb.requirement: Disclose (1) the total number of notices of food safety violation received and (2) the percentage corrected; and (1) the number of recalls issued and (2) the total amount of food product recalled.
issb.gap: P9.E4 counts voluntary and forced recalls with reasons but not the quantity recalled. FSSAI notices appear only if material under Reg 30 (P1.E2) or as regulatory action on product safety (P9.E6); there is no count of notices or % corrected.
issb.investorNote: Recall frequency and size are direct indicators of food-safety control and cost exposure.

issb.title: Health & nutrition: revenue and product management
issb.requirement: Disclose revenue from products labelled or marketed to promote health and nutrition attributes, and the process to identify and manage products and ingredients related to nutritional and health concerns among consumers.
issb.gap: No BRSR equivalent. P9.E2 (share of turnover carrying information on safe and responsible usage) is not a nutrition metric.
issb.investorNote: Shifts toward healthier diets and regulation of foods high in fat, sugar and salt are a demand risk and opportunity for snack makers.

issb.ref: SASB FB-PF-270a.1 to FB-PF-270a.4 (IFRS S1 para 55)
issb.title: Product labelling & marketing
issb.requirement: Disclose the percentage of advertising impressions made on children (and on children promoting products that meet dietary guidelines); revenue from products labelled as containing GMOs and as non-GMO; incidents of non-compliance with industry or regulatory labelling and/or marketing codes; and monetary losses from legal proceedings on labelling or marketing.
issb.gap: BRSR counts consumer complaints on advertising and unfair trade practices (P9.E3), corrective actions (P9.E6), product information beyond the mandate (P9.L4) and material fines (P1.E2). It has no children's advertising metric, no GMO revenue split and no count of non-compliance with FSSAI labelling rules or the ASCI code.
issb.investorNote: Labelling and marketing breaches bring fines, forced relabelling and reputational damage with consumers and retailers.

issb.title: Packaging lifecycle management
issb.requirement: Disclose (1) total weight of packaging, (2) percentage made from recycled and/or renewable materials and (3) percentage that is recyclable, reusable and/or compostable, and strategies to reduce the environmental impact of packaging throughout its lifecycle.
issb.gap: BRSR covers EPR applicability and reclaim processes (P2.E3-E4), recycled input share by value for all materials (P2.L3), reclaimed tonnes (P2.L4-L5) and own-site plastic waste (P6.E9). It does not ask for total packaging weight placed on the market or packaging-specific recycled content and recyclability; EPR filings under the Plastic Waste Management Rules hold the weight data.
issb.investorNote: Multilayer snack packaging faces rising EPR costs and recyclability mandates that investors want quantified.

issb.title: Environmental & social impacts of ingredient supply chain
issb.requirement: Disclose the percentage of food ingredients sourced that are certified to third-party environmental and/or social standards (by standard), and suppliers' social and environmental responsibility audit non-conformance rate and corrective action rate (major and minor).
issb.gap: P2.E2(b) gives the % of inputs sourced sustainably without a prescribed definition or split by certification standard. The value-chain assessment indicators give % of partners assessed by value, not non-conformance or corrective-action rates.
issb.investorNote: Ingredient supply chains carry deforestation, labour and traceability risks that buyers and lenders now screen.

issb.ref: SASB FB-PF-440a.1, FB-PF-440a.2 (IFRS S2 Industry-based Guidance)
issb.title: Ingredient sourcing: water stress and priority ingredients
issb.requirement: Disclose the percentage of food ingredients sourced from regions with High or Extremely High Baseline Water Stress, and a list of priority food ingredients with a discussion of sourcing risks from environmental and social considerations.
issb.gap: BRSR has no water-stress sourcing metric and no priority-ingredient list. A.26 may describe sourcing risk qualitatively if it is a material issue; P2.E2 covers sustainable-sourcing procedures only.
issb.investorNote: Climate-driven yield and price shocks in key crops (potato, edible oils, pulses, spices for snacks) hit margins directly.

issb.title: Activity metrics: weight of products sold, number of facilities
issb.requirement: Disclose the weight of products sold and the number of production facilities, used to normalise the topic metrics.
issb.gap: A.18 gives the number of plants (national / international). Weight of products sold is not asked; BRSR physical-output intensities (P6.E1, E3, E7, E9) use an entity-chosen output measure that may be production rather than sales.
issb.investorNote: Activity metrics let investors normalise footprints and compare companies of different size.
